Saʿīd ibn Abī al-Ḥasan said: "He struggles with the calamities of this world and the hardships of the Hereafter."

Qatādah said: "He struggles with the affairs of this world and the Hereafter, so you will never find him except in hardship."

meaning in hardship and difficulty. This resembles His saying: ﴿We created them and strengthened their joints (asrahum)﴾.

So this oath includes the exaltation of His House and His Messenger.

This is an independent proof, and it includes the recompense whose basis is power and knowledge. So his deeds of good and evil are counted for him, and He has power over him to recompense him with what he deserves.

Then He, glorified is He, denounced man's saying: ﴿He says, "I have squandered wealth in abundance."﴾ Lubadan is the abundant that is piled up, one part upon another. This man boasts of squandering it and spending it in other than its proper ways. Had he spent it in the ways He commanded and placed it where it belongs, it would not be squandering; it would be a means of drawing near to Allah and reaching His pleasure and reward. Thus He denounced his boasting and vanity at spending wealth on his desires and aims, where spending is in fact a ruin for him.

Then He rebuked him with His saying: ﴿Does he think that no one has seen him?﴾ Here He used "lam," which denotes the past, in correspondence with His saying: ﴿He says, "I have squandered wealth in abundance."﴾ For that refers to the past: does he think that no one saw him in what he spent and what he squandered?

(Section)

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Nay, I swear by this city.﴾

There is no place on the face of the earth for which every able person is obliged to strive to it and circumambulate the House within it other than it, and there is no place on the face of the earth whose kissing and touching is legislated and in which sins and burdens are removed other than the Black Stone and the Yemeni Corner. It is established from the Prophet ﷺ that prayer in the Masjid al-Ḥarām is worth one hundred thousand prayers. In Sunan al-Nasāʾī and al-Musnad, with a sound chain, from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Zubayr, from the Prophet ﷺ, that he said:

"A prayer in this mosque of mine is better than a thousand prayers elsewhere, except the Masjid al-Ḥarām; and a prayer in the Masjid al-Ḥarām is better than a prayer in this mosque of mine by one hundred prayers."

Ibn Ḥibbān also narrated it in his Ṣaḥīḥ.

This is explicit that the Masjid al-Ḥarām is the best of the places on earth absolutely. For this reason, setting out for it (shadd al-riḥāl) is obligatory, while for other places it is recommended but not obligatory. In al-Musnad, al-Tirmidhī, and al-Nasāʾī, from ʿAbdullāh ibn ʿAdī ibn al-Ḥamrāʾ, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while standing on his mount at al-Ḥazwarah in Makkah, saying:

"By Allah, you are the best land of Allah and the most beloved land of Allah to Allah; and had I not been expelled from you, I would not have left."

al-Tirmidhī said: this is a ḥasan ṣaḥīḥ ḥadīth.

Moreover, among its distinctive features is that it is the qiblah for all the people of the earth; there is no other qiblah on the face of the earth.

Also among its distinctive features is that facing it or turning one's back to it while relieving oneself is prohibited, unlike the rest of the places on earth.

Then he mentioned a hypothetical proof that He, glorified is He, is more deserving of being seen and more worthy than this servant who has two eyes with which he sees. How then would He give sight to one who does not see? And how would He give him the instruments of expression, the two lips and the tongue, so that he speaks and clarifies what is in his soul, and commands and forbids, while He Himself does not speak, does not address, does not converse, does not command, and does not forbid? Is the perfection of the created being derived from anything other than the perfection of its Creator?

And whoever made another knowing of the two paths of good and evil, which are the two ways of them (al-najdayn), is He not more deserving and worthier of knowledge than that other?

And whoever guided him to these two paths, how would it be fitting for Him to leave him aimless, not knowing what harms him and what benefits him in his livelihood and in his return?

And are prophethood and messengership anything other than for perfecting the guidance to the two paths?

Thus all of this points to the affirmation of the Creator, the attributes of His perfection, the truthfulness of His messengers and of His promise.

These are the fundamentals of faith upon which all the messengers agreed, from the first of them to the last. When a person reflects upon his own state and his creation, he finds it to be among the greatest proofs of their soundness and their establishment. His own reflection upon himself and his creation suffices him. The messengers were sent as reminders of what is in the natural disposition (fitra) and the intellects, and as completers of it, so that the proof of God would be established against the servant through his natural disposition and through His message. Despite this, the proof was established against him, and he did not storm the steep path (al-'aqaba) that lies between him and his Lord, which he cannot reach until he storms it by doing good to His creation: freeing a neck, meaning releasing it from bondage, so that God may free him from the bondage of his own self and the bondage of his enemy; and feeding an orphan or a needy person on a day of hunger; and by sincerity toward Him, glorified is He, through faith, which is His pure right upon him, meaning affirming His report, obeying His command, and seeking His face; and by advising others, that he enjoin upon them patience and compassion, and accept the advice of whoever enjoins these upon him, so that he is a patient and compassionate person in himself and a helper to others in patience and compassion. Whoever does not storm this steep path and perishes before it, perishes cut off from his Lord, not reaching Him, but rather veiled from Him.

People are of two kinds: the successful, who is the one who crossed the steep path and got beyond it, and the perishing, who is the one who remains behind the steep path, and they are the majority of creation. None storms this steep path except the lean, for it is a steep, arduous ascent that none crosses except one light of burden. They are the companions of the right (ashab al-maymana), and the perishing who remain behind the steep path are those who did not affirm the report and did not obey the command. They are ﴿the companions of the left, upon them is a fire closed over﴾.

It has closed over them, so they cannot come out of it, just as the works of error and false beliefs that contradict what His messengers reported have closed over them, so their hearts did not come out of them. Likewise this fire has closed over them, so their bodies cannot come out of it.

Reflect upon this surah, despite its brevity, and upon what it contains of the subjects of knowledge and faith. And success is from God.

Also, the method of the Qur'an is to mention knowledge and power as a warning and intimidation, because recompense follows from them, as the Exalted said: ﴿Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you﴾.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays? Have you seen if he is upon guidance, or enjoins righteousness? Have you seen if he denies and turns away? Does he not know that Allah sees?﴾

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And say, "Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and His messenger and the believers."﴾

And He said: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private talk? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording.﴾

This is very abundant in the Qur'an, and the purpose is not merely the report of power and knowledge, but the report together with what follows from them of recompense and of justice. For when He is powerful, it is possible to requite them, and when He is knowing, that can be done with equity and justice. Whoever is not powerful, it is not possible to requite him.

And if one is powerful but does not know the details of deeds and the measures of their recompense, he will not be recompensed with justice.

The Lord, exalted is He, is described with complete power and complete knowledge, so recompense from Him depends solely upon His will and His choice. Therefore the intelligent person must seek salvation from Him through sincerity and good conduct. This is the storming of the steep path, which includes repentance to God, exalted is He, and doing good to His creation.

And He said: ﴿Then he did not storm the steep path﴾. It is a past-tense verb, and "la" (not) was not repeated with it, either because the particle "la" is used in this way, like the use of "ma," or because this verb is treated as a supplication, as in: "fa-la salima" (so may he not be safe), "wa-la 'ash" (and may he not live), and similar expressions. Or because the steep path has been explained as a collection of matters, so storming it is the doing of each one of them, and that makes repeating it unnecessary; it is as if He said: "Then he did not free a neck, nor feed, nor was he among those who believed."

The reading of the one who reads ﴿fakku raqabah﴾ (freeing a neck) with the verb appears more preferable than the reading of the one who reads it as a verbal noun, because His saying ﴿And what will make you know what the steep path is?﴾ follows the pattern of His saying ﴿And what will make you know what the Reality is?﴾, ﴿And what will make you know what the Day of Recompense is?﴾, ﴿And what will make you know what it is? A blazing fire﴾, and their like, to glorify the status of the steep path and magnify its matter. Whoever does them has stormed the steep path.

Also, whoever reads it as a verbal noun with an added genitive must supply an omission, namely: "And what will make you know what the storming of the steep path is? And if correspondence is attained in meaning, its attainment both verbally and in meaning is more complete and better.

This is also the view of Abu 'Ubaydah.

Al-Kalbi said: "It is a steep path between Paradise and the Fire."

This is also the view of Muqatil, that it is the steep path of Hell.

Mujahid and al-Dahhak said: "It is the Sirat, which is laid over Hell."

This is perhaps also the view of al-Kalbi. And the view of these is sounder in reasoning, in transmission, and in language.

Also, the method of the Qur'an is to mention knowledge and power as a warning and intimidation, because recompense follows from them, as the Exalted said: ﴿Say: He is able to send upon you a punishment from above you﴾.

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Have you seen the one who forbids a servant when he prays? Have you seen if he is upon guidance, or enjoins righteousness? Have you seen if he denies and turns away? Does he not know that Allah sees?﴾

And His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And say, "Work, for Allah will see your deeds, and His messenger and the believers."﴾

And He said: ﴿Or do they think that We do not hear their secret and their private talk? Yes, and Our messengers are with them, recording.﴾

This is very abundant in the Qur'an, and the purpose is not merely the report of power and knowledge, but the report together with what follows from them of recompense and of justice. For when He is powerful, it is possible to requite them, and when He is knowing, that can be done with equity and justice. Whoever is not powerful, it is not possible to requite him.

And if one is powerful but does not know the details of deeds and the measures of their recompense, he will not be recompensed with justice.

The Lord, exalted is He, is described with complete power and complete knowledge, so recompense from Him depends solely upon His will and His choice. Therefore the intelligent person must seek salvation from Him through sincerity and good conduct. This is the storming of the steep path, which includes repentance to God, exalted is He, and doing good to His creation.

And He said: ﴿Then he did not storm the steep path﴾. It is a past-tense verb, and "la" (not) was not repeated with it, either because the particle "la" is used in this way, like the use of "ma," or because this verb is treated as a supplication, as in: "fa-la salima" (so may he not be safe), "wa-la 'ash" (and may he not live), and similar expressions. Then he mentioned a hypothetical proof that He, glorified is He, is more deserving of being seen and more worthy than this servant who has two eyes with which he sees. How then would He give sight to one who does not see? And how would He give him the instruments of expression, the two lips and the tongue, so that he speaks and clarifies what is in his soul, and commands and forbids, while He Himself does not speak, does not address, does not converse, does not command, and does not forbid? Is the perfection of the created being derived from anything other than the perfection of its Creator?

And whoever made another knowing of the two paths of good and evil, which are the two ways of them (al-najdayn), is He not more deserving and worthier of knowledge than that other?

And whoever guided him to these two paths, how would it be fitting for Him to leave him aimless, not knowing what harms him and what benefits him in his livelihood and in his return?

And are prophethood and messengership anything other than for perfecting the guidance to the two paths?

These are the fundamentals of faith upon which all the messengers agreed, from the first of them to the last.
